current_episode.title: Architect Career: Salary, Training & What the Job Is Really Like

guest.bio_context: Rob Dupont attended Syracuse University from 1985 to 1990 for a five-year architecture program and obtained his bachelor's degree. He worked as an apprentice under architect Robert Young in Kingston before establishing his own practice during an economic slowdown around 1991-1992. He has been practicing architecture for over 40 years and has built extensive networks with builders, engineers, and contractors, which has led to consistent work and referrals.

context.real_quote: If you're prepared to work and not make a lot of money at the beginning and you love what you do, then be an architect. If you don't love it, don't do it.
key_stats: Architect's license renewal requirement: valid for 3 years then must renew with fee
License reciprocity fee to practice in another state: $200-$300
Rob's first summer job wage: $5 per hour (40 years ago)
Starting salary for licensed architect in Baltimore-DC area (when Rob was established): approximately $30,000 per year
Current starting wage for architecture students in Boston area: $20 per hour
Current starting wage for recent architecture graduates in Boston area: $25 per hour
Rob Dupont career timeline: approximately 40+ years practicing architecture
Economic slowdown period prompting Rob to go independent: around 1991-1992
Rob's plan to retire: approximately 8 more years remaining in practice

pending_qa.q: What is Rob Dupont's preferred architectural style?
pending_qa.r: Rob prefers the language of modernism—cement, less ornamentation, lots of glazing, glass, and open spaces with light. While he will design in any style the client wants and has worked on traditional and modern buildings, modernism is what aesthetically appeals to him most.
